problem: The native foreground transaction published text and its durable root progress, but left the serving executor watermark behind. Its visibility wait replayed the same text record again.

evidence.note: Candidate-only Debug operation attribution on a shared host; no reference reruns or throughput claim.

change: Successful owned native publication adopts the selected full-text workers’ committed sequence during infallible activation, under the original catalog/apply lifetime fence.
Manual visibility waits now observe that committed frontier instead of replaying it. Progress adoption does not persist, reclaim, allocate or deliver callbacks under the publisher locks.

Threaded registrations receive an atomic committed frontier. Their worker drains superseded private sessions before changing its mutable replay/persisted frontier; source capture/apply checks reject superseded work.

Threaded waits omit redundant forced persistence only when the atomic publisher certified that registration’s complete applied frontier. Ordinary persisted watermarks still take the forced visibility callback.
Physical retirement and credit return remain on the existing consumer retirement path; adoption alone never retires retained data.

coverage: manual progress adoption does not replay or persist and does not retire early
threaded publication racing a stale source capture
ordinary forced visibility persistence and cleanup failures
pause, retry, resource and backlog ownership
native indexed exports retain owned eligibility after reopen
one checkpoint plus updated serving replay watermark
validation.scope: Manual C API paths; the later threaded-only fixes are covered by the expanded runtime gate.

qualification: The full architecture and current-candidate performance qualification are still incomplete. A rebuilt live Debug diagnostic is next.
